symptom: `describe page M.P` prints Forms$DataGrid, Forms$ReferenceSelector, Forms$DropDown, Forms$InputReferenceSetSelector as `-- NOT re-executable` comments, and `exec` of that output replaces the page with the widgets gone — `Replaced page M.P`, no warning, mx check clean on both sides (found on a Mendix 10.24 MPR v1 app)
cause: execCreatePageV3 / execCreateSnippetV3 / execCreateLayout rebuild the document from the statement, and a widget MDL cannot author can never be in the statement; describe's NOT re-executable note was the only signal, and it is a comment the parser discards
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_pages_rewrite_guard.go` (checkNoUnauthorableWidgetsDropped, validateUnauthorableRewrites), `cmd_pages_describe_dangling.go` (describeDroppedWidget feeds unauthorableSink), `cmd_pages_create_v3.go`, `cmd_pages_layout_v3.go`, `cmd_pages_describe.go` (layout body through describeWidgetBody); tests `mdl/executor/issue1622_page_rewrite_unauthorable_test.go`
insight: A describe note that says 'NOT re-executable' is a promise the executor never read: the comment is dropped by the parser, so the warning lives only in the file the user is about to run. Make the describer the single source of what a rewrite loses — describeDroppedWidget already ran for exactly the unauthorable widgets — and have the rewrite describe the stored document into io.Discard and refuse on that list, rather than keeping a second list of authorable $Types that would drift from the describe switch (the staticimage finding is that drift). Exempt any widget the statement declares by name, or a widget the builder can write but describe cannot print refuses its own script. No fixture holds these widgets (grep of testdata finds none), so seed one into a real stored unit with UpdateRawUnit — the #1459 test's legacyDataGridBSON is the Studio Pro shape — and test at exec, check -p and the ALTER-drop escape hatch. Enumerate the rebuild call sites: snippets and layouts take the same builder; layout describe had to be routed through describeWidgetBody before the sink could see it
